commenti.body:
There will never be another apocalypse now.
Someone would have to be insane to even try to re-capture that lightning in a bottle, and you’d be better off just making a different version of hearts of darkness. I feel pretty secure about that pick

2001, a modern version of it wouldn’t work at all. Part of the reason it’s such a great film is because it’s so ahead of time technically and thematically, and that such a masterpiece could come out from one mind. If someone was to remake it, it wouldn’t have that human substance or impressiveness since the things done in that film are quite easy with today’s technology.

I think all of Fellini movies could never be remade. Nothing could ever capture his energy or style, or that of his actors. Guilietta Masina and Marcello Mastroianni: can you imagine ANYONE trying to take on their roles? Impossible. Don’t even bother to try.

Any and all films should be remade if someone wants to do it and can convince the rights owners to let them do it. 

Handwringing over remakes is baffling to me. Just don’t watch it. To this day I still haven’t watched the Robocop remake and most of the time don’t even remember it exists. 

It doesn’t matter. If some mad lad wants to remake Citizen Kane, let them cook. It could somehow be good. Or we all just ignore it forever. No muss no fuss.
Princess Bride is a perfect film and I don’t think it’s possible to remake it in a way that gets even a fraction of the charm it did. From the cast to the sets and costumes it’s a 10/10.

Back to the Future. The Bobs have said it will never be remade or get a sequel as long as they’re alive. Hopefully they can structure their wills so that nobody can remake it after they pass either. It’s a perfect film, perfect cast, perfect script, perfect direction, music, cinematography, editing…. Anyone attempting to remake it will fail miserably

To be sure, it is a spoof so doesn't quite count... But Bicycle Thieves was of course the principal basis The Icicle Thief. I wouldn't say it can quite count as a proper remake for several reasons, but all the same , if nothing else it immediately came to mind when I saw that on the list given to prime discussion.
Does Bob Fosse's version of Nights of Cabria, Sweet Charity, count?

>Any and all films should be remade if someone wants to do it and can convince the rights owners to let them do it. 

OP actually says almost exactly what you said. Their question is asking what movies what movies we just think will never get remade. I don't see any handwringing being done here.
I don’t see them being remade. But to expand the franchise is probably money on the table for a studio.

It was kind of remade during the pandemic, and it's really, really cool.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lR8pA\_WV9QI
That’s less a remake imo and is more classified as an homage.

Likewise there are plenty of remakes, or second attempts at adaptations, that are leaps and bounds better than the original. People often forget that the 1939 Wizard of Oz was the second attempt at that story. The first came out im 1925 and even by standards of the day it was pretty bad. Lord of the Rings was theatrically released in theaters as an animated film in the 70s. True Grit, CODA, The Departed, Magnificent Seven, The Thing, and A Star Is Born are all remakes off the top of my head that the original was the first movie, and they are all still good. They do something the original doesn't and therefore serves a purpose to stand alongside the original on the American film catelogue
It was indeed extremely painful and probably Day Lewis’ worst role, kinda proving OP’s point.
His Girl Friday was the second film adaptation of The Front Page, as well.
